title: One Minute Changes: Speed up A–D chord changes
summary: The video introduces the One Minute Changes exercise, a speed-focused drill that alternates between two chords (A and D) for one minute to build faster, smoother chord changes. It emphasizes anchoring a finger, tolerating some inaccuracy early on, and using a timer while counting each change aloud to quantify progress. The instructor differentiates One Minute Changes from Chord Perfect Practice (speed vs. tonal accuracy) and suggests practical targets: around 30 changes per minute as a pass threshold and 60 changes per minute as a long-term goal, with the expectation that some chord changes will be harder than others. The video also promotes supplementary tools (a practice routine generator and a One Minute Changes counter app) and references left-handed practice (Nitsuj lessons) as a relatable starting point for beginners. Viewers are encouraged to log progress and discuss results in the comments.

sections.description: This section lays out the core exercise: pick two chords (A and D), use an anchor finger, and change between them as many times as possible in one minute. It discusses pain management in early stages, the importance of speed for playability, and the distinction between rapid changes (One Minute Changes) and improving chord tone (Chord Perfect Practice). It also introduces tracking progress by counting changes, and mentions tools for practice organization and progress tracking, plus a nod to left-handed practice as a demonstration of beginner struggles.
